_comment: DSHOT300 twin of four_channel_bidirectional_600.json: identical except for the speed. MATCHED PAIR with four_channel_unidirectional_300.json: the same duration (20 s), arm window, poll_ms (10), DSHOT300, motors, hardware and throttle profile (all four channels hold throttle 215 for the whole run; 0 to that value is a single step after arming); the ONLY difference is that this file's motors are bidirectional (replies are read; the expect thresholds judge them: CRC-valid share, median eRPM, longest wait between new captures; min_record_rate_hz is left out because with a 10 ms poll the pass rate is capped near 100 per second and has not been measured). Compare the two and the difference is the protocol. Channels 1 and 2 share PIO block 0 (sm0/rx1 and sm2/rx3), channels 3 and 4 share PIO block 1 (sm4/rx5 and sm6/rx7); two bidirectional motors may share a block, a unidirectional one may not (so the unidirectional file uses one state machine per channel).
